item.title: The Witcher 4 Will Be a GTA 6-Sized Leap Forward, CD Projekt Red Says
item.description: We're living in a post- Grand Theft Auto 6 world now, meaning that almost every other game in development will inevitably be compared to Rockstar Games' new open-world crime drama. The developer behind two other big open-world brands, The Witcher and Cyberpunk, is now fielding questions about how its future games will stack up against GTA 6 .

item.title: Why the Spurs believe Pelicans guard Jeremiah Fears intentionally tripped De'Aaron Fox
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) and New Orleans Pelicans guard Jeremiah Fears (0) get into an altercation during the second quarter of an NBA game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) PORTLAND, Ore. - Victor Wembanyama missed his first game of the season Monday in Sacramento. De'Aaron Fox missed his second. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson saw a silver lining in the former absence. The latter was another matter. Fox was sidelined with a right shin contusion suffered two nights earlier against New Orleans, on a play Johnson believed crossed the line. With 46 seconds remaining in the first quarter of Saturday's 114-91 victory over the Pelicans , Fox was cutting through the lane when Jeremiah Fears stuck out a leg and struck the All-Star guard in the shin. "From my perspective, it looked like he got tripped," Johnson said. "I wasn't a huge fan of seeing that play when it happened on tape. Now he has to miss a game because of it." Johnson indicated the Spurs have submitted video of the play to the NBA office for review, though further disciplinary action appears unlikely. With Fox out and guard Dylan Harper missing his third consecutive game with a hip strain, the Spurs opted to keep Wembanyama sidelined against the Kings as well. The official designation for Wembanyama's ailment was "lower back tightness." His absence allowed the Spurs to work on what has been their greatest weakness during a 15-3 start to the season - learning how to function when their All-Star center is off the floor. De'Aaron Fox is out tonight against the Kings with a right shin contusion, coach Mitch Johnson pointed out in the pregame press conference that it was caused by this incident where Jeremiah Fears appears to intentionally trip Fox as he runs past him Via: https://t.co/PdISIJbzR4 https://t.co/lcUo0CQgcK - MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 24, 2026 Even without Wembanyama and two-thirds of their starting backcourt, the Spurs found a long-awaited answer Monday, digging deep for a 123-107 victory over the moribund Kings. "The more you can get those reps and see what it looks like and see longer stretches to work through the stages of that, it's very helpful," said Luke Kornet, who started in Wembanyama's place and posted his first double-double of the season with 18 points and 11 rebounds. "Hopefully we can carry that forward." San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) drives down the court during an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Johnson is hopeful the Spurs won't have to go much longer without their two All-Stars. There is a good chance one or both could return for Wednesday's NBA Cup game in Portland. "Optimistic both should not be (out) long term," Johnson said. "I haven't gotten far enough into it to start looking into the crystal ball for Portland." Rookies shine for sho

item.title: The USMNT needs Copa América. What it doesn't need is another home game
item.description: USA fans look on from the stands during the CONMEBOL Copa America match between the United States and Boliva on June 23, 2024 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Copa América, South American soccer’s pride and joy, is returning to the U.S. in 2028 because organizers remain spellbound by the ticket sales and marketing success of the 2024 edition here. Tuesday’s announcement is a positive development for the U.S. team, which, for competitive reasons, desperately needs a break from the monotony of CONCACAF before the 2030 World Cup. Only so much is gained from fiddling with neighbors over and over again. Assuming the U.S. qualifies next summer, Copa América will furnish its to-be-announced head coach with pressure-packed, consequential matches in a prestigious tournament against different types of opponents. That’s a welcome change from the Nations Leagues and biennial Gold Cups, which are starting to feel like watching “Friends” reruns on Nick at Nite. But here’s where this Copa news falls short for the U.S. program: It’s in the U.S. again. Yes, the team needs to play in Copa América, but what it really needs is to play in it in South America. It needs to step out of its comfort zone of sterile hotels and stadiums. It needs to say goodbye to family and friends, experience new training and playing environments, and feel the heat of stepping into Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã or Buenos Aires’ El Monumental to play the host team. True, the U.S. often feels like the visiting team at home when it tangles with Latin American opponents boasting a passionate diaspora. But the players still enjoy the predictability of home logistics, travel patterns, security and general nationwide support. That is not what they need right now. They need to suffer. Consider this: The U.S. hardly ever plays outside its borders, an arrangement that many might argue has left the program soft heading into World Cups. Talent, tactics and such are part of why the U.S. has stumbled in the round of 16 in its past four appearances, but mental toughness in the pressure-cookers of knockout soccer can’t be dismissed either. The location of matches is often out of the U.S.’s control. For revenue purposes, CONCACAF has staged every Nations League final four and almost every Gold Cup in the States. CONMEBOL, which oversees South American soccer, has shifted Copa América — the oldest international tournament in the world — to the U.S. three of the past five times after staging the first 44 editions in its own continent. The U.S. does have a say in the location of friendlies. Here again, though, the team is not facing the rigors of playing away matches. It has played 16 consecutive friendlies in FIFA windows at home since a visit to Mexico in October 2024. Going back to 2022, the number grows to 28 of 31. item.title: Koepka’s Return Shifts FedEx Cup Status For Three Players
item.description: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images Brooks Koepka’s return to the PGA Tour has triggered a specific ripple effect through the final FedEx Cup standings. The five-time major champion came back this year under the “Returning Member Program” after securing his exit from a LIV Golf contract. His presence on the field created a unique mathematical situation for players waiting just outside the top 125. With Koepka ending at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup, three other golfers advanced one position in the final rankings. This adjustment was necessary because the tour did not want Koepka to negatively impact another player’s eligibility for the 2027 season. The shift changed the status of Jason Day, Max McGreevy, and Pontus Nyholm. Jason Day climbs one rank to No. 110, securing conditional status within a category that stays fixed throughout the year with no reshuffle. Day also holds the option to choose a career money exemption based on this adjustment. At the RSM Classic, Max McGreevy tied for 10th and just missed the top 125 required for conditional status. With Koepka positioned ahead of him, McGreevy now sits at No. 125, securing the final spot in that tier. Pontus Nyholm sees the most dramatic change, jumping from No. 151 with no status at all to conditional status at No. 150. According to the Associated Press, David Skinns, Seamus Power, and A.J. Ewart also took advantage of the two-player field addition stipulation but did not see their standings change enough to alter their eligibility. How the Returning Member Program Works The mechanics behind this shift rely on specific rules established for players returning from LIV Golf. When Koepka entered the field, the tour added two players each time he played to ensure the field size remained consistent. These additions allowed players like Skinns, Power, and Ewart to earn points they otherwise would not have collected. Skinns earned 38 points in a single event, while Power collected 28 points across two events. Ewart secured 27 points in one appearance. These numbers helped them in their own right, but the primary impact was on the players directly behind Koepka in the standings. The tour prioritized fairness for those on the bubble, ensuring that a returning player’s presence did not push a competitor out of a playing category they had worked hard to reach. Context From the Season-End Drama The RSM Classic on Monday provided the backdrop for these final calculations, featuring a dramatic four-man playoff that also determined status for other players. Reaching No. 64 in the standings, Penge jumped just beyond the top 50-60 group that secured spots in the first two signature events. He entered the playoff at No. 120, well outside the top 100 required for full playing status. item.title: Scarlett Schremmer Disqualified From Annika Debut After Lying
item.description: Michael Madrid-Imagn Images The 19-year-old University of Miami sophomore received a rare sponsor exemption to The Annika driven by Gainbridge, only to disqualify herself by lying about a yardage book. She claimed she never used the illegal green-reading material when officials first asked, but photographic evidence proved otherwise. Golfmagic reported the disqualification came Saturday after the tour saw clear images of her consulting the prohibited book during the round. The book itself was legal in college golf, which explains why it sat in her bag, but it carries zero weight on the professional tour. Schremmer missed the cut before the ruling dropped, yet the lie turned a missed opportunity into a scandal. Her mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, caddied for her, adding a layer of personal pressure that clearly backfired. Social media saw playing partner Perrine Delacour publicly challenge the tournament’s rule breach handling, causing the situation to become messy. The Lie That Sealed Her Fate Officials were alerted to the issue after the opening round, yet Schremmer kept playing on Friday before the truth came out. She initially told officials the book was not in use, a claim she later admitted was false in a Friday Instagram post. Schremmer wrote, “I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal Information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use.” That panic cost her the chance to show her skills against the best women in the world. Delacour, who partnered Schremmer for the first two rounds, took to X to ask, “Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies.” The French veteran confirmed she spoke directly to rules officials about the violation, highlighting how the amateur status of the invitee complicated the situation. The LPGA Tour stated the rule requires players to use only approved books throughout their round, and photo evidence showed Schremmer violated that mandate. Trust Is Hard To Build Back With two fall college tournament wins and a USGA 2026 Elite Amateur Program spot secured, Schremmer held the 51st rank in the World Amateur Golf Ranking. Those credentials meant nothing once she chose to hide the truth. While Schremmer’s Friday admission signaled a move from denial to accountability, the harm remains irreversible. She stated in her post, according to Yahoo, “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

item.title: Measles death toll rises to 14 as national case tally nears 6,000
item.description: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a young child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

item.title: 'Go be somewhere else': Steelers legend challenges DK Metcalf
item.description: Credit: The Pivot Sports After a strong start to the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have lost back-to-back games coming off the bye, and star receiver DK Metcalf is once again sucking up oxygen around the team in on-field confrontations. During Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Metcalf was ejected for poking Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. The incident came after key drops and a build-up of physicality with the Philadelphia secondary throughout the game. Metcalf had just one reception for 2 yards, his third time in the past four contests with two or fewer catches. The former Seahawk is set to make $38-plus million starting next season, putting a glaring spotlight on his lack of productivity and professionalism and leading former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin to check Metcalf on Sunday Night Football after the ejection. During an episode of The Pivot Sports to start the week, fellow Steelers great Ryan Clark added to the criticism of Metcalf, calling out the star for his lack of “emotional regulation” and questioning whether Metcalf was long for Pittsburgh. “Why do we have to be the guy that can’t control himself? That has no professional maturity. That doesn’t understand emotional regulation,” Clark said. “Then you get disqualified, and you shake your head.” Clark showed several of Metcalf’s earlier miscues in the game, contrasting the star’s lack of focus with how his backup, Max Hurleman, played as well as the clutch performance of Philadelphia’s DeVonta Smith on the other side. Clark emphasized how much Metcalf’s mistakes cost the team. “Maybe throw hands when you’re getting locked up. Maybe throw hands when you’re trying to get a block. Maybe throw hands when it’s 3rd-and-4, and you need to get four yards. But you want to do it after the play?” Clark said. “Slapping the referee, that doesn’t make you a bad man. That makes you a man that eventually goes home.” The incident with DeJean also opened Metcalf and the Steelers up to media chatter and off-field distractions . Later, Clark highlighted numerous Steelers greats from the team’s two Super Bowl runs in the late 2000s and early 2010s, challenging Metcalf to match their mental toughness and leadership. “Most of the games, they were all available. And what they did was lead,” he said. “They would never walk out on their team after being kicked out of a game, without hearing what the coach had to say, without hearing what their teammates had to say. Be accountable, DK. Lead, DK. Be the person that they brought you over there to be. And if not, go be somewhere else.” To make matters worse for the Steelers, after acquiring Metcalf, the team ultimately turned him into the replacement for former Pittsburgh draft pick George Pickens. While Metcalf continues to tally distracting screw-ups during games, Pickens is on his way to a second straight 1,000-plus-yard season for a dominant Dallas Cowboys offense. item.title: Referees’ chief Howard Webb breaks ranks with surprise verdict as Man United win Leny Yoro appeal
item.description: Referees’ chief Howard Webb breaks ranks with surprise verdict as Man United win Leny Yoro appeal Manchester United successfully managed to overturn the red card that was dished out to Leny Yoro against Liverpool on Sunday, but referees’ chief Howard Webb has a different view of the situation. United win appeal Earlier today, it was confirmed that Yoro’s red card at Anfield has been overturned by the Football Association. Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes of United’s humiliating 4-0 loss to bitter rivals Liverpool. The Frenchman ran into the back of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool striker raced through on goal and cut across his path. Yoro was consequently given his marching orders. Liverpool went on to take the lead from the resulting free-kick, and from that point United struggled badly, barely laying a glove on the hosts, who were lifted by their numerical advantage. A furious Mauricio Pochettino didn’t shy away from blasting the decision to dismiss Yoro . Pochettino argued that Yoro didn’t intentionally bring down Yoro. He even pointed to another similar incident in which Jeremy Jacquet brought down Bryan Mbeumo but escaped punishment. United will take some solace from the fact that Yoro will be available to face Brentford this weekend. But Webb has insisted that Yoro’s red card was “certainly not wrong.” every Frenchman to play for Manchester United Source: Wikipedia and API-Football Surprising verdict Webb, Chief Refereeing Officer of Pro Ref, said on the Mic’D Up show , “Firstly, i want to say, I think this is a really decisive decision by the referee, Sam Barrott. We know it’s clearly a foul. I don’t think there’s any dispute about that.” “And we also know that it’s outside the penalty area. we’re thinking about the sanction, aren’t we That’ why we’re talking about this.” “Is it a denial of an obvious goal scoring opportunity? Four considerations officials have to think about. direction of play, it’s definitely going towards the goal. It’s not going out wide. Proximity from goal, well, it’ just outside the penalty area. the location of other defenders. Well, there’s only Yoro there. The keeper is moving back towards his own goal.” Webb continued, “He has to put the brakes on and possibly come back out. the reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration, that’s control or likelihood of keeping on or gaining control of the ball. Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro.” “He’s moving at pace at that moment, and a foul comes in and knocks him down.” “And there’s a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Senne Lammens. It's the latest in a grueling fight over a major spying rule that hasn't technically lapsed. item.title: Tsunami RT Brings Porsche To IMSA GTD Class For 2027 Season
item.description: Manthey racing�s Porsche 911 (911) is a blur of speed up from turn 5 during practice at the Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix Featuring IMSA, Friday, July 31, 2026, at Road America near Elkhart Lake, Wis. Tsunami RT is heading to the United States to race. The San Marino-based team will field a Porsche 911 GT3 R in the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup starting in 2027. This move brings a new name to the GTD class and adds depth to the five-race schedule. Team principal Valerio M. Speziali wants to build a lasting presence in North America. He sees the US market as a place to grow the team’s skills over time. “We are delighted to join the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup next year, giving us the chance to build our experience and grow in endurance racing season by season,” Speziali said, according to Speedway Digest . The group knows the competition is fierce, but they are not backing down. “We know how competitive the GTD field is and we’re ready to fight for strong results from the opening round,” he added according to Speedway Digest. A Driver Mix Built for Endurance The car will carry the number 79 and feature a mix of veterans and fresh talent. Fabio Babini leads the group with deep roots in IMSA history. He won the GTU class at the 2000 Rolex 24 and took the GT title at Le Mans in 2001. His last start in the WeatherTech Championship was back in 2019, but he knows the track well. Matteo Cressoni brings recent experience with 13 starts between 2015 and 2025 in various GT cars. Two new faces will make their debut in 2027. Alex Fontana and Johannes Zelger have raced together for Tsunami RT in the Intercontinental GT Challenge during the 2026 season. The team will rotate drivers based on the race length. They plan to use a three-driver lineup for the Sebring, Glen, Road America, and Road Atlanta events. This strategy helps manage the physical toll of long races while keeping speed high. Adding a new Porsche entry changes the dynamic of the GTD class. The field is already crowded with top-tier teams, and every new car adds pressure. Babini’s resume shows the team is not just playing for participation. He has won at the highest levels of sports car racing. His experience in the GRAND-AM series and American Le Mans Series gives the team a solid foundation. Cressoni has also seen action in Ferrari and Lamborghini entries, proving he can handle different machines. The Rolex 24 holds special weight for this organization. Speziali called the chance to see the team on the entry list a major milestone. It is not just about finishing the race. It is about proving that a European team can succeed in the tough US endurance scene. The 2027 season will show if they have the pace to match the big names. According to Speedway Digest, the 2027 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship will mark Tsunami RT’s debut with a Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) competing across the five-race IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup schedule.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers is Hurting the Steelers’ Season
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers lost 19-16 to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The loss extends the Steelers’ losing streak in Philadelphia, with their last win coming in 1965. The Eagles squashed the Steelers’ running game, holding Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle to under 30 yards each. On the flip side, Saquon Barkley gashed the defense for a 38-yard touchdown, giving the Eagles a 13-0 lead in the first quarter. Edge rusher Alex Highsmith exited with an ankle injury, which head coach Mike McCarthy said could sideline him against the Denver Broncos on Friday. SAQUON HOUSE CALL! pic.twitter.com/e009d6X5H5 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 22, 2026 This is the second straight week the Steelers’ offense has started slowly. Losing guard Mason McCormick last week certainly did not help, especially against the Eagles’ stout defensive front. Still, the defense held Philly to six points after the first quarter. The offense had plenty of chances to close the gap, but failed to. There is enough blame to go around when talking about the Steelers’ recent offensive failures: Receivers not getting consistently open, McCarthy’s playcalling bizarrely excluding running back Jaylen Warren, and the offensive line having its worst stretch of the season. However, one player is single-handedly sinking the Steelers’ season with his performance coming off the bye. Aaron Rodgers . Rodgers Cannot See the Field Well In the last few weeks, Rodgers has had genuine issues finding open receivers, especially when the running game hasn’t taken off. The Steelers had plenty of touchdown opportunities with a few red zone trips. Rodgers was right in saying that “scoring threes is not usually a winning formula” at the start of his post-game presser . It starts with him. End zone look at this play. Looks right after snap, presumably to hold safety. Look how much space Jaylen Warren has though on the angle route. Still, Rodgers has to hit this to Germie Bernard. It's there. He knew it, too. https://t.co/c2AJTYpnvs pic.twitter.com/dlLipPZpg7 — Josh Carney (@ByJoshCarney) November 23, 2026 One of these mistakes came late in an 8-minute drive near the end of the first half. First & Goal, the Steelers have an empty set with Warren lined up on the right. Rodgers throws to Germie Bernard , but misses him high in the middle. It wasn’t a terrible look, but Warren’s angle route left him completely open underneath. A touchdown here would have put the Steelers within six, but Rodgers’ recurring issue of opting for harder throws and missing open guys kept them to field goals. A touchdown would have massively shifted momentum, especially after Robert Spears-Jennings punched the ball out during Philly’s kickoff return to start the second half. Unfortunately, this turnover also led to a kick after more misthrows. Taking Too Long to Snap the Ball An underrated issue with the Steelers offense, particularly on the road, is late snaps. item.title: Oilers’ Ryan Nugent-Hopkins details difficult stretch behind five-game absence
item.description: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is ready to return after missing five games with an issue that continued bothering him during Edmonton’s recent road trip. The Edmonton Oilers forward addressed his absence before facing the Vegas Golden Knights . Speaking to NHL reporters, Nugent-Hopkins explained that something happened near the end of Edmonton’s game in Toronto. He spent the following week dealing with the problem before the team cleared him to return. “I feel good now. Something kind of happened near the end in Toronto, and just kind of was battling that all week and dealing with that,” Nugent-Hopkins said . MORE: NHL analyst Elliotte Friedman defends cancer survivor after Canadian anthem mishap He also suggested the issue might have started with an earlier puck impact. “Maybe it led from a couple weeks ago with the puck, but just stuck around on the road on a long road trip, not playing any games,” he added. The forward admitted that missing games was difficult, although staying around his teammates helped. “But nice to be around the guys at least,” Nugent-Hopkins said. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins explains why he needed more recovery time Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; The Edmonton Oilers celebrate a goal scored by forward Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (93) at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) When asked whether head-related injuries can create complications, Nugent-Hopkins explained why players sometimes need additional recovery time. “I feel like it happens a decent amount of time, and you can talk yourself into feeling really good, and sometimes there’s more behind the scenes going on,” he said. He acknowledged the frustration but emphasized the importance of taking the necessary time. “It’s unfortunate. You got to be able to take your time, and but I feel really good now, and ready to go for sure,” Nugent-Hopkins added. His return gives Edmonton another important option in its forward group. The veteran has recorded 11 points, including four goals and seven assists, across 12 appearances this season. Seven of those points have come on the power play, highlighting his value on special teams. MORE: Wayne Gretzky sees no comparison between Connor McDavid & other NHL stars The Oilers have also relied heavily on Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl for offensive production. Nugent-Hopkins provides another experienced playmaker who can support their top-six attack. His availability should help Edmonton regain some consistency. However, the team will need to manage his workload carefully after two injury interruptions this season. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Gul breaks Villa's resistance in scrappy Galatasaray win
item.description: UEFA Champions League Galatasaray 1 - 0 Aston Villa FT Deniz Gul scored his first goal of the season having joined Galatasaray from Porto in the summer [Getty Images] Deniz Gul's late winner sunk battling Aston Villa at Galatasaray as Unai Emery's men slipped to successive Champions League defeats. The substitute nodded in with 13 minutes left to break Villa's resistance, scoring with the game's first effort on target. It settled a scrappy match and dented Villa's top-eight ambitions, with Emery's side having lost in Barcelona earlier this month. Villa knew victory in Turkey - as they returned to Istanbul for the first time since winning the Europa League in May - would put them on track to reach the knockout stages automatically. But defeats leaves their hopes in the balance and they now face tough home games against champions Paris St-Germain on 8 December before Borussia Dortmund come to Villa Park in January, with Villa then finishing the league phase at Slavia Prague. They are now winless in six games in all competitions having failed to score in four of them. Emery would initially have been satisfied how his team handled the surface - after much debate about the condition of the pitch - and the atmosphere at the RAMS Stadium. Without star striker Victor Osimhen, sidelined with a knee injury, the hosts struggled for a focal point allowing Tyrone Mings and Victor Lindelof to comfortably hold off any muted attacks. Yet Villa themselves struggled to create until Ian Maatsen was thwarted by some desperate home defending early in the second half. It was Villa's best and only chance as the hosts took control and snatched the winner when Gul pounced after Villa failed to clear a corner. Aston Villa ratings Zion Suzuki: Alert to the hosts' long balls and did not have a meaningful save to make until he was beaten by Gul's header. 6 Taylor Harwood-Bellis: A first Champions League appearance for the defender, initially left out of the European squad, and handled himself well at right-back. 7 Victor Lindelof: Rarely troubled in the first half with Galatasaray missing Osimhen up front and needed to remain resilient after the break but Gul broke the deadlock. 6 Tyrone MIngs: A first start since the end of October and the hosts played to his strengths before they turned up the pressure, which Villa could not deal with. 6 Ian Maatsen : Tried to get forward when he could and had Villa's best opening but was on the back foot for much of the second half. 6 Boubacar Kamara: Eventually withdrawn as Villa chased a leveller having been unable to help his side keep control after the break. 6 Joao Gomes: A solid performance after being recalled to the starting line up, although was booked in the second half for a petulant kick on Yunus Akgun. 6 Alysson: The winger is earning Unai Emery's trust with a seventh start in Villa's past nine games. item.title: ‘I’m actually glad I got fired’: Dave Portnoy says Michigan has hit rock bottom and coach ‘belongs in a nursing home’
item.description: Dave Portnoy on the sideline before kickoff of the first half between Michigan and Oklahoma at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. The University of Michigan announced Tuesday that, despite earlier reports that it had landed Trev Alberts as its next athletic director, it ultimately decided not to proceed with the hire. “The University of Michigan’s search for its next athletic director is ongoing,” Michigan spokesperson Paul Corliss said in a statement. “As we navigate a rapidly changing landscape in intercollegiate athletics, the values that define Michigan will guide our decisions and reinforce our commitment to excellence and integrity, both in the classroom and in competition.” Michigan’s regents reportedly decided that Alberts wasn’t the right choice after immersing themselves in the details of a 2024 lawsuit at Nebraska involving an inappropriate relationship between a basketball coach and a player. However, Alberts had already signed a binding MOU and will receive a $17.3 million from the school. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, a Michigan alum and superfan, reacted to the news in a video on social media. “We’ve hit rock bottom. We’re a laughingstock. Michigan, the University of Michigan, has become a laughingstock. No other way to say it,” Portnoy said. This video is for Michigan fans and Michigan fans eyes only https://t.co/QKIEAUitpX — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) November 24, 2026 “I’m actually glad I got fired from Big Noon Kickoff because I don’t have to go on there and have tomatoes thrown at me. Oh, there’s the laughingstock. There’s the Michigan man. I don’t know what the h*ll they’re doing. It started, Sherrone Moore, last year, f*cking the team manager, butter knife, police chase, eyes on p*ssy, not football. “And this year, we suck. We get Whittingham, who belongs in a nursing home, watching Matlock, who still thinks he’s playing at Rice-Eccles Stadium, doesn’t even know who Ohio State is. We suck.” Portnoy then touched on the news surrounding Alberts. “We hired Trev Alberts to be our next AD, sign a letter of intent with him. And then we decide we don’t want Trev Alberts because he didn’t pass some test or something. It’s like Trev Alberts has jumped school. School. You don’t know about Trev Alberts? We owe Trev Alberts $17 million. We got to pay his full buyout. The guy didn’t work a day. A day. He didn’t work 30 seconds. “We owe him $17 million. We had to fire Jason Beck. We owe him $9 million. Whittingham’s going to be third. What are we doing? What has become of this school? We are a laughingstock. People see this Block M and me walking down the street; they laugh, they point, they go, there’s the clown… “How do you owe a guy $17 million who didn’t work a minute? And I know they’re going to say there’s a clause in the contract that he didn’t pass, that you— did you not do an ounce of research? Why are you signing this before now? It’s going to be a lawsuit. We’re going to— what are we doing?”

item.title: Phillies offseason is looking bleak after missing out on Teruaki Sato
item.description: Phillies offseason is looking bleak after missing out on Teruaki Sato originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Two days before Thanksgiving, the Philadelphia Phillies have not made a significant roster move of any kind. The December 1 lockout is looming, and the Phillies are beginning to run out of time to make moves. But it's not just the time crunch making things tricky for the Phillies. They've already lost out on Teruaki Sato, easily the best free-agent option the Phillies could've landed this Fall. He's headed to the Chicago Cubs on a six-year, $120 million deal. After missing out on Sato, what now for the Phillies' offseason plans? The Athletic's Charlotte Varnes and Matt Gelb shared an update on just that, and it's looking like the Phillies could be in for quite the bleak offseason. Phillies might be in for a bleak offseason after missing out on Teruaki Sato After missing out on Sato, it would seem natural for the Phillies to look towards Seiya Suzuki and/or Randy Arozarena as free-agent outfield options. But, as The Athletic duo pointed out, there are problems with both. "The Phillies would have to sacrifice draft picks and international bonus money to sign either outfielder because both were extended qualifying offers," Varnes and Gelb write. "They may wait to sign until the labor situation is resolved." There's just one problem with that line of thinking: "If Arozarena's market develops in the next week, though, the Phillies will not have the luxury of waiting," Varnes and Gelb write. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news Between the loss of draft picks and international bonus pool money, and the potentially rushed nature of a Suzuki or Arozarena deal, the Phillies might not be the landing spots for either right-handed hitting outfielder. So, if they aren't a perfect suitor for an outfielder, what about a pitcher to upgrade the bullpen? Unfortunately, things aren't looking good there either. "They could focus on pitching, but the Phillies, according to multiple league sources, are not considered serious players for the top free-agent reliever, Adrian Morejon," Gelb and Varnes report. Adrian Morejon would've been an awesome pickup as a setup man for Jhoan Duran. But a deal isn't looking likely. With issues signing someone like Suzuki or Arozarena, and their lack of strong interest in Morejon, what could they actually do this offseason? MORE : Full contract details on Tarik Skubal’s reported $450M deal with Mets Signing a veteran to a one-year deal, as they've done before, might be the thing Dave Dombrowski falls back on. Trading for players might prove tricky, as The Athletic duo notes the Phillies "will be protective of their top prospects." Thanks to their weaker farm system as seen by the rest of MLB, if the Phillies aren't willing to part with their top prospects, getting a trade through for a good player isn't very likely

item.title: Blue Jays land Japanese star pitcher Kaima Taira on $80M deal
item.description: Blue Jays signing The Blue Jays landed a starting pitcher for roughly one-sixth the price of Tarik Skubal. After losing to the Mets in the Skubal sweepstakes, the Blue Jays pivoted and are signing Japanese righty Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million deal, The Post’s Jon Heyman first reported . The deal includes an opt-out clause after the third year, per Heyman. Kaima Taira of the Seibu Lions celebrates setting an NPB record with 39 consecutive scoreless games in Fukuoka, Japan, Thursday, July 1, 2021. /Kyodo News via AP The starting pitching dominos are falling in free agency ahead of the expected Dec. 1 lockout, with Skubal serving as the catalyst by signing his nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets . The Blue Jays made a competitive nine-year, $420 million offer for Skuba l, but he opted for $30 million more to head to Flushing. Freddy Peralta agreed to a five-year, $125 million deal with the Orioles on Tuesday, and the pitching-needy Blue Jays swooped in to land the talented 27-year-old Taira. Taira has experience as a reliever and starter, and spent the past season with the Seibu Lions of the Japan Pacific League as a starter. He posted a 1.54 ERA spanning 23 outings, pitching 146 innings and striking out 141 batters. Taira walked 45 batters but allowed just four homers. The year prior, he made 54 appearances and tallied 52 2/3 innings while posting a 2.05 ERA. He owns a career 1.85 ERA in his nine seasons pitching in Japan, according to Baseball Reference. “His stuff and release characteristics are what is intriguing to evaluators. His fastball sits 94-97 mph and hits 100 mph with his four-seam fastball, the headliner in an eight-pitch mix: sinker, changeup, splitter, cutter, slider, sweeper, and curveball,” according to ESPN . “Taira achieves a unique low release and advantageous angle for his fastball with his outlier extension (roughly a foot more than his 5-foot-8 stature) and lower than average arm slot.” The Blue Jays now have a solid rotation featuring AL Cy Young runner-up Dylan Cease, Taira, midseason trade acquisition righty Joel Soriano and talented youngster Trey Yesavage. They reportedly are also in the mix for offensive help and their representatives met with Jazz Chisholm Jr. earlier in free agency. Toronto finished in last place in the AL East last year following its run to the World Series in 2025.

item.title: Local Insider Remains Convinced Pohlads Will Sell Twins
item.description: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect This offseason has gotten off to a busy start for the Minnesota Twins. Although a lockout appears to be looming , that hasn’t stopped Tom Pohlad from backing up his talk when it comes to spending money. Ryan Jeffers secured the first windfall of cash by accepting the qualifying offer at $23.15 million for 2027. Sonny Gray then returned to the franchise on a two-year deal worth $55 million. What portion of those salaries will be paid remains to be seen. It’s also possible that the Pohlads won’t be the ones writing the checks after all. Walters still expects Pohlads to sell the Minnesota Twins After the 2024 season, the Pohlads gave Minnesota Twins fans the best news in years. They were exploring a sale . Then they pulled the team off the market before Tom Pohlad took over for his younger brother Joe. Since then, Tom has been adamant about the family’s plan to re-invest in the organization in ways that those before him have not. He has also downplayed any plans to put the team back up for sale after a new Collective Bargaining Agreement is reached. However, local insider Charley Walters (Pioneer Press) remains convinced that is the ultimate endgame. I remain convinced that once baseball settles on a new labor deal, the Twins will be sold. The Pohlad ownership “explored” _ their word _ a sale in October of 2024 before announcing in August of 2025 the team would remain under their control. No doubt Twins’ ownership figures a new labor contract that will include major TV deals across the league will be worth a lot more than the $1.75 billion they quietly sought last year, probably even more than $2 billion. The Twins scenario is not unlike Angels’ owner Arte Moreno announcing in 2022 that he was “exploring” a potential sale, then pulling the team off the market a year later. Then, last September, he agreed to sell for a record $4 billion. Charley Walters – Don’t Print That Related: Don’t Laugh. MN Twins Remain Committed to Spending… Everything about the timeline Walters outlines makes sense. The Pohlads would be exceptionally interested in a Major League Baseball world where owners get their way and a salary cap is instituted. Even with a floor, capped expenses would drive valuations through the roof. With a new CBA, the Pohlads could fetch a valuation that would far surpass the $1.75 billion they sought while carrying massive debt . If the 2027 season isn’t played at all, there would be little to no revenue for the team. Expenses would be just as muted, though, and player salaries would not hit the bottom line. That all factors into the balance sheet when weighing what a sale could look like once the sport resumes. MN Twins sale remains best-case scenario Regardless of how big Tom Pohlad talks or how much money he spends now, many fans would welcome the family’s departure. item.title: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions
item.description: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions Fran Soto, president of Spain’s Technical Committee of Referees (CTA), has expressed his desire to improve relations with Real Madrid amid ongoing tensions. Los Blancos have been vociferous in their complaints about the refereeing in Spain as well as the Negreira scandal involving Barcelona, leading to a lot of tension between the club and the governing bodies. Soto wants to move on from the Negreira scandal Speaking to the media at the first Refereeing Gala, Soto addressed the ongoing tensions surrounding the refereeing in Spain and Real Madrid’s complaints, in particular. The CTA president defended the refereeing community over the fallout from the Negreira scandal and called for the focus to shift towards restoring normality. “The referees are the ones most harmed by a person who was vice president of the Technical Committee of Referees,” Soto said, as quoted by SPORT . Real Madrid are unhappy with the refereeing in Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Soto insisted that officials have suffered the consequences of the controversy and argued that they cannot remain trapped by events from the past. ”We mustn’t dwell on the past; we have to move forward and continue refereeing, put it behind us, and look to the future,” he added. Soto questions Real Madrid’s VAR statistics Soto was also asked about the presentation made by Real Madrid during the club’s recent assembly , wherein they showed that VAR had ruled out 42 of their goals since the technology was introduced, compared to 19 for Barcelona. Real Madrid president Florentino Perez used the figures to reinforce the club’s complaints about what it considers unfavourable refereeing treatment. Real Madrid have made multiple complaints over the officiating. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) Soto declined to engage in a direct confrontation with Real Madrid but questioned whether the figures, on their own, could support the conclusions being drawn. “Every club defends its position. I don’t agree that this objective data can be used to draw conclusions,” he stated. However, the CTA president made clear that he has no intention of escalating the dispute and would prefer to see communication between the two sides return to normal. “I don’t want to get into a dispute with any club, least of all with Madrid. I hope that in the future we can resolve this situation,” he concluded.

item.title: Giants get timeline on Greg Newsome II injury with pressure now on Paulson Adebo
item.description: Greg Newsome; Paulson Adebo Greg Newsome II is going to miss more than just his revenge game. Newsome is expected to miss at least the next four games and could be pressed to return before the end of the regular season after a high ankle sprain that requires tightrope surgery , The Post confirmed. The Giants have seven games in seven weeks remaining. The high end of his timeline is six weeks on the sideline. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW Newsome has not yet been placed on injured reserve, which would sideline him for at least four games and create a roster spot needed to elevate practice-squad contributor defensive lineman Duane Smoot. The Giants have now lost four defensive starters for long periods of time, including season-ending injuries to edge Brian Burns, linebacker Tremaine Edmunds and defensive lineman Chauncey Golston. It makes Newsome’s recent decision to sign a three-year, $45.75 million contract extension rather than play out the rest of his walk year look wise. Had Newsome finished the season injured or playing at a lesser level through pain and then entered free agency, he might have been asked to accept another prove-it deal. Without Newsome, the Giants will turn to benched former starter Paulson Adebo (four passes defended and an interception in place of Newsome against the Jaguars) to start next to Deonte Banks, who is having the best year of his career as he nears free agency. It’s a toss-up whether Banks or Newsome would be considered the Giants’ No. 1 cornerback as both have had shutdown moments this season. New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II (20) reacts on the field during a game against the Arizona Cardinals in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. Bill Kostroun for NY Post New York Giants wide receiver Malachi Fields (88) and cornerback Paulson Adebo (21) walk off the field after a game at MetLife Stadium in Brooklyn, N.Y., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: IMSA Cuts Testing Days: A Smart Move For The 2027 Season
item.description: The No. 52 LMP2 Inter Europol ORECA of Nick Boulle and Tom Dolman drives through the Carousel during the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Sunday, August 4, 2024, at Road America in Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect IMSA is finally cutting the fat off the testing schedule for the 2027 WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. The new sporting regulations announced Tuesday hit the top teams the hardest, but they might be exactly what the series needs to level the playing field. The rules eliminate all private testing for GTD Pro entries outside of sanctioned events. GTP teams now get only two manufacturer test days per season, with team-specific days removed entirely. According to Sportscar365 , these restrictions come alongside new licensed tests at Sebring and Road Atlanta that are open to every team. The move stops deep-pocketed teams from hoarding track time and forces everyone to rely on their actual race strategy. Inter Europol Doubles Down Anyway While the rulebook tightens, one team is betting big on its own talent. For the 2027 season, Inter Europol Competition revealed plans to run two full-time ORECA LMP2 07 entries. This expansion adds a second car to their existing No. 43 program, creating a formidable two-car assault on the title. The team manager, Sascha Fassbender, said, “We are very happy to have two cars committed to the full IMSA season with two strong driver lineups.” Inter Europol is not backing down from the challenge despite the reduced testing window. The team aims to fight for the championship with both cars, building on a close 2026 title race. Following their second-place finish last year, Jeremy Clarke and Tom Dillmann are back for the flagship No. 43 car. Clarke noted their drive to win, stating, “We came so close last year, so we’re even more motivated to finish on the top step at the end of the season.” Testing Limits Will Test Team Depth The new regulations also slash test days for LMP2 and GTD teams, cutting LMP2 allocation from 12 days down to eight. GTD teams see their days drop from six to two, though FIA Bronze-rated drivers still get two extra days. According to Sportscar365, private testing is now banned during a 120-day blackout period preceding major events like Daytona and Sebring. This forces teams to be sharper with their limited track time. Inter Europol’s new No. 343 entry brings in fresh firepower with drivers Nick Yelloly and Daniel Goldburg. Goldburg brings experience from racing against the team for three years in LMP2. He summed up his move to the organization with a simple phrase: “If you can’t beat them, join them.” The team has also added INDYCAR driver Nolan Siegel for the Rolex 24 at Daytona lineup. The 2027 season will start with a sanctioned test at Daytona International Speedway on December 10 and 11.

item.title: Mystery grows over ex-Met, actor Lance Broadway’s sudden death after police report: ‘Unexplained’
item.description: Lance Broadway The police report related to Lance Broadway’s death is providing far more questions about the former Mets pitcher and Hollywood actor’s passing than it is answers. Broadway died at 43 years old on Nov. 17 in an apartment complex stairwell in Dallas, Texas, and law enforcement appears to be stumped by how he ended up that way, according to a Dallas Police Department incident report obtained by the California Post on Tuesday. Actor Lance Broadway arrives at a special screening of “The Iceman” at ArcLight Hollywood in Hollywood, California, Monday, April 22, 2013. Getty Images Authorities called the matter an “unexplained death (no offense)” in the document, adding that there were no signs that Broadway was under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The “narrative information” section of the report was heavily redacted, though it did note that the person who reported the situation to cops observed Broadway “to be deceased sitting on the stairwell of the call location.” Lance Broadway of the New York Mets walks back to the mound against the Atlanta Braves in New York, Monday, Sept. 21, 2009. Jeff Zelevansky Police were called to the scene at 5:56 p.m., according to the incident report, and Broadway was formally pronounced dead at 6:20 p.m., per the Dallas County Medical Examiner. The cause of death remains undetermined as autopsy results are still pending, the Dallas County Medical Examiner stated. Lance Broadway #41 of the Chicago White Sox pitches during a game against the Kansas City Royals at U.S. Cellular Field in Chicago, Aug. 14, 2008. MLB Photos via Getty Images Broadway, a first-round pick in the 2005 MLB draft, pitched for the White Sox and Mets from 2007 to 2009, and in retirement, he got into acting. The 6-foot-2 right-handed pitcher garnered roles in several popular movies and TV shows, including “Olympus Has Fallen,” “Lucifer” and “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.”

item.title: 'It's impossible to make an analysis' - Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca admits Mauricio Pochettino's Man Utd are a mystery ahead of Champions League clash
item.description: Fenerbahce v OL Lyonnes - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play-Offs First Leg - Getty Images Sport Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca says it is "impossible to make an analysis" of Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash in Lisbon. With Leny Yoro sent off after eight minutes at Anfield, Fonseca has turned to footage of Pochettino's time with the United States, while refusing to label the Red Devils "fragile". Fonseca in the dark over Pochettino's United Fonseca has admitted he has little to go on when preparing for United, with Pochettino having taken charge of only one game. That match, a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, was disrupted by Yoro's early red card, which has since been overturned on appeal. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," Fonseca said, as reported by BBC Sport . "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." Fonseca refuses to label United 'fragile' Despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Fonseca refused to accept that they are vulnerable. "I don't follow the reasoning," he said. "Manchester is a great team. I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile." He pointed to United's last Champions League outing, when they came from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day," he added. United's domestic slump United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their last six matches, leaving Pochettino with a huge task after replacing Michael Carrick during the international break. Fonseca, who was appointed on November 4 after Sporting bought him out of his contract at Lyon, is also new to his role and has had little time to stamp his own ideas on the side. Defender Eduardo Quaresma has already warned his team-mates against underestimating United . Lisbon showdown awaits Sporting host United at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday night, with Yoro cleared to play. Pochettino will be desperate for a positive result to ease the pressure after a chaotic start to his reign.

item.title: Detroit Lions lose rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard for the season
item.description: The Detroit Lions have lost another player to a season-ending injury on their defense. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 24, that rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard will miss the rest of the season after injuring his knee in last week’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Gill-Howard was hurt on a goal-line offensive snap, where’s he’s played at times as a jumbo tight end this season, late in the game. “Hate that for him,” Campbell said. “He’s had a heck of a season up to this point.” A sixth-round pick out of Texas Tech, Gill-Howard has played as the Lions’ No. 3 defensive tackle this season and been one of their best interior pass rushers. He has 11 tackles, six quarterback hits and two sacks. Gill-Howard’s injury is the second major setback on the defensive line and third to the unit this month. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell is out for the season with a spinal cord injury he suffered in a Nov. 1 win over the Minnesota Vikings, and Pro Bowl defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore the ACL in his right knee while celebrating a sack in the Lions’ win over the New England Patriots in Germany two weeks ago. Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Gill-Howard have played the bulk of the snaps at defensive tackle for the Lions this season, but Campbell said he’s confident in the team’s depth at the position. Big ends Tyler Lacy and Levi Onwuzurike can play inside, Mekhi Wingo could see his first action of the season and practice squad linemen Aidan Keanaaina and Taki Taimani are candidates to play in the Lions’ Thanksgiving game this week against the Chicago Bears. The Lions and Bears are 8-2 and ties for first place in the NFC North. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Detroit Lions lose rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard for the season

item.title: “100%” – Liverpool receive boost in race for €50m January signing
item.description: “100%” – Liverpool receive boost in race for €50m January signing Alejandro Balde Transfer Latest: Liverpool Monitoring Barcelona Exit as €50m January Fee Emerges Liverpool are among the clubs tracking Alejandro Balde ahead of the January transfer window, with fresh reporting indicating the Barcelona left-back is expected to leave and could cost as much as €50 million. The update comes via Juan Jesus, who states: “Despite Deco’s words, Alejandro Balde is 100% out. Several clubs know this and are closely monitoring his situation, including Manchester United, PSG, AC Milan and Liverpool,” before adding, “Barça expects the bidding to drive up the price and is confident of securing his departure for at least 45-50 million euros.” That information places Liverpool firmly in the conversation around one of the more intriguing defensive situations developing before the market reopens. Balde has long been viewed as a high-level talent, and any indication that Barcelona are prepared to sanction a sale will naturally alert a number of elite sides across Europe. Liverpool transfer plans sharpen into focus For Liverpool, the key question is whether genuine interest turns into concrete action. Recruitment decisions under Andoni Iraola are likely to be framed by need, timing and value, and Balde sits at the intersection of all three. He is young, established at a major club, and carries the profile of a player who could develop further in the Premier League. At the same time, the reported valuation changes the complexion of the discussion. A deal once viewed in some quarters as a market opportunity now looks more like a premium investment. Barcelona, if this update is accurate, appear confident that interest from multiple clubs will create competitive tension and strengthen their negotiating position. Liverpool will have to decide whether a fee in the region of €45 million to €50 million represents the right use of resources in January. That is especially relevant in a window where flexibility can be limited and where clubs tend to prioritise positions of immediate urgency. Barcelona stance raises stakes on Balde The most striking element in this latest development is the certainty around Barcelona’s intention. If Balde is indeed heading for the exit, attention will shift quickly from speculation to structure, with suitors weighing up transfer fee, wage demands and the player’s own preferences. There is no shortage of competition mentioned in the report, and that matters. Manchester United, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan all being credited with interest suggests Liverpool would not be operating in a clear run. In those circumstances, discipline becomes crucial. Liverpool have shown in previous windows that they are prepared to step away when valuations move beyond their internal comfort zone. Balde’s appeal is understandable. He offers athleticism, recovery speed and upside, and those qualities tend to retain value in the modern market. Barcelona may therefor

item.title: Man United star opens the door to surprise January exit
item.description: Man United star opens the door to surprise January exit Ayden Heaven Open to Manchester United Exit as Loan Interest Grows Amid Relegation Fears Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to leaving Old Trafford in January, with a loan move currently viewed as the most realistic outcome as concern grows over his role and development. According to BBC Sport , the 20-year-old is weighing his options while United continue to struggle near the foot of the Premier League table. Heaven’s situation has become increasingly delicate. The centre-back was an unused substitute in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, a result that underlined the scale of the task facing new head coach Mauricio Pochettino. The report states that Heaven is worried about what United’s position in the relegation zone could mean for his progress. This is a player now working under his third manager in 21 months since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025. It is understood he recognises that Pochettino may favour senior options as United attempt to avoid what the report describes as a “shock relegation”. Loan Move Emerging as Likely Outcome Heaven’s preference is believed to be a temporary exit, though the report adds that he would also consider permanent offers. Fulham and Barcelona are both credited with previous interest, and both had attempted to sign him when he chose to leave Arsenal. Photo IMAGO United’s own transfer plans may further shape the picture. The club have been strongly linked with a move for another central defender in January, with Fulham’s Calvin Bassey among the names mentioned. That said, Fulham regard Bassey as important and are not encouraging interest. Game Time Fears at Old Trafford At United, Heaven has mainly been used as a back-up option. He enjoyed a spell in the side under Ruben Amorim, then fell out of the team under Michael Carrick. Last season, he returned only when an injury crisis opened the door. His versatility remains a plus, he can operate at centre-back, left-back and in midfield, yet there appears little expectation that he will be trusted as a regular starter while instability continues and United sit 19th in the league. Heaven remains under contract until 2029, with an option for an extra year, so United retain control, but the player’s willingness to explore a move is a notable development at a difficult moment for the club. Our View This is exactly what happens when a club loses any sense of direction. A talented young defender arrives, shows enough to suggest he can contribute, then gets dragged through a cycle of chaos, managerial changes and panic decisions. Three managers in 21 months tells its own story. Nobody can pretend this is a stable environment for development. If Ayden Heaven is looking around and thinking this mess could damage his future, he is absolutely right. United are 19th in the league, just took a 4-0 hammering at Liverpool, and the immediate response is more uncertainty about who stays, who plays and who

item.title: Why this insider loves Freddy Peralta’s fit with Orioles
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Why this insider loves Freddy Peralta’s fit with Orioles appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Baltimore Orioles signed free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta after helping the Tampa Bay Rays get to the World Series, the sports world has been praising the move for its fit. With Peralta now heading to the Orioles , this MLB insider speaks on why the fit is great. Peralta started the 2026 season with the New York Mets, but recorded a 4.99 ERA with 113 strikeouts and a 5-9 record in 22 starts before being traded to the Rays, where he finished the season with a 3.25 ERA with 43 strikeouts and a 5-2 record in 10 games. Also providing some great outings in the postseason, Jon Morosi spoke on MLB Network about how he raised his stock in Tampa Bay. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “[The Rays] helped him rejuvenate his stock entering the off-season, and very importantly, the fact that he was traded at midseason did a couple things. Yes, it allowed him to regain that fastball and regain the moxie; his overall repertoire seemed to tick up in that Rays uniform,” Morosi said. More on how this MLB insider loves Freddy Peralta to the Orioles Morosi would call the signing in retrospect a swap since the Orioles lost starting pitcher Trevor Rogers to the Chicago Cubs on a five-year, $120 million deal, as Baltimore got Peralta on a five-year, $125 million contract. However, Morosi went into more detail about how other variables make him “love the fit.” “It also means that because Peralta did not have a draft pick attached to him, they did not lose a pick, and in fact they gained a pick from the Cubs by virtue of that move,” Morosi said. “So in general, you like the way that things are going now for the Baltimore Orioles and for the Cubs as well, for that matter. But I thought Peralta, who has now had some success in the American League East with the Rays, you love the fit. Really, really strong contract too for Peralta and his representatives.” It remains to be seen what other moves the Orioles make after getting Peralta, as the team looks to improve after finishing at 79-82, putting them fourth in the AL East. item.title: How Does Kaima Taira Fit On Blue Jays After $80 Million Deal?
item.description: Toronto Blue Jays executive vice president and general manager Ross Atkins The Toronto Blue Jays have reportedly agreed to a five-year, $80 million deal with Japanese pitcher Kaima Taira, per MLB insider Ken Rosenthal . Taira's deal also reportedly includes an opt-out after the third year, and according to Mitch Bannon , he is getting a $5 million signing bonus. The big news is the fact that the Blue Jays finally landed a starting pitcher. They were reportedly involved in trying to sign Freddy Peralta, Tarik Skubal and Trevor Rogers. Taira has been pitching in Nippon Professional Baseball since 2019. The 27-year-old has spent most of his time as a reliever, but has two campaigns as a starter under his belt. He served as a starter last season, winning the Pacific League ERA title. It's safe to assume that he will have a chance to round out the Blue Jays' rotation after posting a 1.36 ERA and 141 strikeouts last season. He has had great success out of the bullpen as well, though, throughout his career. The Blue Jays already have Dylan Cease, Trey Yesavage and José Soriano locked into the rotation. They will have Cody Ponce back as well. He was the 2025 KBO MVP and signed a three-year, $30 million deal with the Blue Jays in the offseason, but tore his ACL in his first game. Taira has a chance to be the No. 5 starter with his new deal, and he has the potential to exceed expectations. He has an eight-pitch mix and has a fastball that averages 95.8 mph. He throws from a low arm slot and relies on his four-seamer, cutter and sweeper against righties. Against lefties, his sweeper takes a backseat to his changeup. The Blue Jays will now likely try to look for some depth in the rotation and bullpen help. As far as the offense goes, they still have a ton of work to do. However, the top free agent hitters are all still available. More MLB: Is Paul Goldschmidt Enough To Fix Mets' First Base Problems?

item.title: Ha-Seong Kim Signs With Detroit Tigers
item.description: Oct 3, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Atlanta Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim (7) walks to the dugout after striking out in the third inning of game one of the NLDS against the Los Angeles Dodgers for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo F… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Ha-Seong Kim and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a $5 million, one-year contract, per Jeff Passan of ESPN. Kim is a bounce-back candidate after enduring two injury-plagued seasons in which he was limited to under 100 games. The team is in a somewhat similar boat as they won just 76 games in 2026 and largely weren’t a factor in the American League Central or the Wild Card race. Both sides will hope that the versatile infielder can get back to playing close to his early MLB career best to help propel a talented but youthful infield. Infielder Ha-Seong Kim and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $5 million contract, sources tell ESPN. — Jeff Passan (@JeffPassan) November 24, 2026 Ha-Seong Kim Is Now A Tiger Ha-Seong Kim can play at shortstop as well as at second and third base, and has generally graded as an above-average defender throughout his career, as evidenced by his 2023 NL Gold Glove for the utility position. Improving infield defense was a target for the team this off-season as the Tigers committed several high-profile errors in September. For example, they committed three errors in one inning on September 16th against the Toronto Blue Jays, leading to a 5-1 loss and the end of a six-game winning streak. Sep 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim (7) hits an RBI single against the Philadelphia Phillies in the eleventh inning at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images While Ha-Seong Kim had a down defensive season in 2026, largely due to injury, he should be back to his best with the glove and therefore able to help this Detroit team. Kim also struggled with the bat in the season just gone, as he hit a miserable .116 in his limited time in Atlanta. However, this is the same Ha-Seong Kim who put up 5.0+ WAR in consecutive seasons in 2022 and 2023, so there is hope that he can be a positive contributor for the Tigers’ offense. The current infield is anchored by defending AL Rookie of the Year Kevin McGonigle at shortstop, with both Hao-Yu Lee and Max Anderson expected to compete for game time at both second and third base. Others, such as John Peck, Javier Baez, or Zach McKinstry, could also compete for innings at either the keystone or the hot corner, and all three, plus Kim, can deputize at short when McGonigle needs a rest. The current mix is fairly green outside of Baez and McKinstry, although neither is expected to play a major role in Detroit barring injuries. The Seong Kim deal also brings into question the future of newly-acquired Tsung Che-Cheng, an infield defensive specialist traded for cash considerations. item.title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State. The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State. It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections. The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.” It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’ The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement. It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern. The MDPCO accused the APC leadership of failing to take decisive action against members allegedly involved in political violence, warning that its silence could further embolden those responsible. “This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition,” it said. The organisation warned that Nigerians would not accept the use of violence or insecurity as instruments of electoral conquest, insisting that political parties must respect citizens’ freedom to choose their leaders. It declared that the resort to violence would not alter what it described as Nigerians’ determination to vote the APC out of power. “The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said. It demanded an immediate end to what it described as attempts to suppress democratic participation, while urging Nigerians to support its principal, Engr. Seyi Makinde

item.title: It was reprisal action – Ughelli LG chairman accuses Omo-Agege’s boys of firing first shot
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Movudu, has described the violence involving Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and his supporters as a reprisal, accusing the senator’s men of killing community members before the incident escalated. Movudu, who had earlier been accused by Omo-Agege of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt on the senator, denied the allegation, claiming that the violence was triggered by the killing of the community’s president-general and other residents. Speaking on Channels Television on Tuesday, the council chairman alleged that Omo-Agege’s supporters fired the first shots, killing members of the community where the senator held his campaign rally. He said the incident was a sad development, extending condolences to victims on both sides of the violence, regardless of their political affiliations. “Let me express my sincere condolences to all those who lost their lives yesterday on both sides. Most of them know to me. They are my friends. Whether they are working for NDC or APC, nobody’s life is worth the ambition of anybody, and it was a sad day yesterday,” he said. Movudu alleged that Omo-Agege had made provocative remarks against him during his campaign visit to the community, claiming that the senator allegedly incited his supporters before they opened fire. He said he was not present at the venue when the campaign took place, as he was in his office, but alleged that Omo-Agege abused him while addressing residents and subsequently riled up his supporters. “But when he was leaving, he riled up the people. He gave instructions to his boys, and then they gunned down the president-general of the community and then shut other people down. It was that death that brought that anger,” Movudu alleged. The council chairman described the subsequent violence as a reprisal for the killing, claiming that the community was angered by the death of its leader and other innocent residents. “What happened yesterday was a reprisal action to answer to the unjust killing of the president and two other onlookers who were innocent,” he said. Reacting to Omo-Agege’s claim that he was targeted for assassination, Movudu questioned the presence of firearms at the senator’s campaign rally, alleging that his supporters were armed. “At the end of it all, he came to TV and was saying that they wanted to kill him. You don’t go to campaign rallies with AK-47. You don’t go to campaign rallies with pump-action rifles. What are you going to use them for?” he asked. Movudu further questioned why supporters attending a political rally would be carrying weapons, alleging that the firearms were used against members of the community. “The people that are going to vote for you, you want to kill them?” he said. His allegations come amid conflicting accounts of the violence, with Omo-Agege accusing Movudu of orchestrating an assassination attempt against him during his campaign visit to Delta community.
