item.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
item.description: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to deliver research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Mission 25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 spacecraft is named in honor of NASA astronaut James “Jim” A. Lovell Jr. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Credit: NASA NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will be on duty during the Cygnus spacecraft’s approach and rendezvous. Watkins will be at the controls of the Canadarm2 robotic arm, ready to capture Cygnus as Delaney monitors the spacecraft’s arrival. Credit: NASA Science highlights In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several new experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions. This research includes: Cardinal Muscle 2.0 Preflight image of the Biocell bioreactor system used to maintain engineered muscle tissue samples as part of the Advancing Therapeutic Treatment of Sarcopenia (Cardinal Muscle 2.0) investigation. Aboard the International Space Station, this investigation tests the effects of potential therapeutics on human muscle cell cultures. The research may help accelerate development of treatments for age-related muscle loss on Earth and support astronaut health during long-duration missions. Credit: Palo Alto Veteran’s Institute for Research Cardinal Muscle 2.0 uses the microgravity environment to explore potential treatments for muscle loss. Muscle atrophy and strength loss experienced by astronauts after spaceflight share many features with age-related muscle decline on Earth and occur more rapidly in microgravity without exercise. Researchers will use a muscle tissue model

item.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
item.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. (2026)) The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower

item.title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The event attracted supporters from the 14 local government areas of the state, including party faithful, women and youth groups, traditional leaders and other political stakeholders. Addressing the gathering, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said voting for the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the state Houses of Assembly, would enable the state to benefit from federal government projects, appointments and other interventions. He argued that Zamfara could not afford to remain in opposition in 2027, urging residents to align with the ruling party at the federal level. “I urge you, the good people of Zamfara, to vote for APC from top to bottom in 2027. Vote for President Tinubu, vote for Governor Lawal, vote for our senators, House of Representatives members and State Assembly members. That is the only way Zamfara will move forward,” Yari said. He also urged voters to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the President as the candidate capable of driving development in the North-West and the country. Yari said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated commitment to addressing insecurity, reviving the economy, improving infrastructure and repositioning the country for sustainable growth. He noted that the North-West, which had experienced years of banditry, kidnapping and economic challenges, needed sustained investment in security and development. “President Tinubu is the only candidate who, if given a second mandate, will develop the North-West and the country at large. He has the vision, the experience and the political will to take Nigeria to the next level. We must give him our full support,” he said. Yari called on Zamfara residents to give Tinubu substantial electoral support in 2027, as they did in 2023, to enable him to complete his reform agenda. He also canvassed support for Governor Lawal’s second-term ambition, saying the governor needed the backing of residents to consolidate his administration’s Rescue Zamfara Agenda. According to him, cooperation between the Federal Government and the Zamfara State Government would accelerate development in security, job creation, education, healthcare and infrastructure. The campaign launch was attended by APC stakeholders, government officials, members of the state executive council, federal and state lawmakers, local government chairmen, women and youth groups, and party supporters. item.title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat. The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area. Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed. The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations. The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North. Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party. “The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none. “We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.” He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled. The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements. Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex. He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas. The post 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
item.description: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States. The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit . After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines. “Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7. item.title: PSC appoints CP Usman Adamu Zamfara Police Commissioner
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State. The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections. According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety. Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police. The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani. item.title: Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins. From custodian to full-service bank Founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025. The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks. The asset manager is the latest in a run of expansions. On Nov. 5, Anchorage Digital Swap Dealer LLC applied to th

item.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
item.description: The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday. CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028. The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final. The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year. “The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.” The host cities and other details will be announced later. “We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani. “We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.” The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. The post ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
item.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. item.title: Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in the Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area of the state. The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, was arrested following reports of repeated grave desecration at the cemetery. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the arrest followed a surveillance operation mounted by the police in collaboration with concerned youths in the community. According to him, on November 10, 2026, at about 7:15 p.m., shortly after the burial of a deceased person, the suspect was allegedly caught digging into the newly covered grave. Usman said vigilant youths apprehended him while he was allegedly committing the act and immediately alerted the police. He added that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons. The police spokesman further said the suspect reportedly admitted involvement in previous acts of grave desecration at the same cemetery, including an earlier incident in which he allegedly removed and took away the burial shroud of a deceased person. Usman said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action. The command commended members of the community for their vigilance and cooperation, while cautioning residents against taking the law into their own hands. It urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities to the police. The post Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, life jackets and other water safety equipment to riverine communities in Bayelsa State following a deadly boat mishap. The House also urged relevant agencies to intensify rescue operations, provide relief materials to affected communities and investigate the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Rodney Ebikebina Ambaiowei, representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, during plenary on Tuesday. Ambaiowei told the House that more than 150 people, mostly indigenes of Southern Ijaw, were involved in the accident on November 20, 2026, while travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a condolence visit. He said the boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan, throwing its occupants into the water. According to him, rescue efforts began immediately, with the Bayelsa State Government, security personnel and other relevant agencies responding to the incident. He disclosed that, as of November 22, several people had been rescued alive with varying degrees of injuries and discomfort, while others had died. The rescued victims, he said, were taken to medical facilities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area and government hospitals in Yenagoa for treatment, while search and rescue operations continued for missing persons and possible survivors. The lawmaker expressed concern that several victims were still missing, despite the efforts of the state government, and called for a broader search operation. He said the tragedy had plunged families and residents of Southern Ijaw, particularly Ukubie and neighbouring communities, into mourning. Ambaiowei attributed the vulnerability of riverine communities partly to the poor condition of boats used for transportation, noting that many were old, overworked and overloaded because of the scarcity of vessels. He also lamented the absence of life jackets, floaters and other water safety equipment, as well as inadequate enforcement of their use, despite waterways being the major means of transportation in the largely riverine constituency. The lawmaker said the communities had limited access to motorable roads, despite ongoing road construction efforts by the Bayelsa State Government, leaving residents heavily dependent on waterways. He warned that failure by the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant bodies to intensify rescue operations and provide relief materials could worsen the impact of the tragedy. Ambaiowei added that the affected communities depended largely on fishing for food and income, stressing that the accident had disrupted their livelihoods and economic activities. He commended President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the affected area to sympathise with families of the deceased. item.title: Bingo on a Global Scale
item.description: Bingo might seem like a fairly simple game, but it’s played in all sorts of different ways around the world. The basic idea is usually the same: match the numbers as they’re called and hope to complete your card before everyone else. But the rules, formats and even the way people play can vary quite a bit depending on where you are. Online bingo has made things even more interesting. Players aren’t restricted to their local halls anymore, and there are plenty of different versions to try without leaving the house. Different Games for Different Tastes Ideally, everyone’s favourite online bingo site would have all the games to cater to all tastes. That means bigger prizes, more games to discover and plenty of social interaction with players from all over the world. And there’s certainly no shortage of choice. In the UK, 90-ball bingo is the traditional favourite. Cards have three rows and nine columns, with players looking to complete one line, two lines or a full house. It’s the format most people associate with a classic bingo night. Across the Atlantic, things are a little different. American bingo usually uses 75 balls and a five-by-five card, with players trying to complete particular patterns. These can include straight lines, diagonals, corners or more complicated shapes. Then there’s 80-ball bingo, which has become popular online. It uses a four-by-four card and offers a middle ground between the British and American formats. It’s quick, straightforward and gives developers plenty of room to come up with different patterns. The Rules Depend on Where You Play Legislation is another area where things can change considerably. In the UK, online bingo operators need a licence from the Gambling Commission and follow rules covering player protection, advertising, identity checks and responsible gambling. There are also specific requirements around how games are operated and how customer funds are handled. Canada takes a different approach with gambling regulation being largely a provincial matter, so the rules depend on where players are located. Ontario has its regulated iGaming market, while Alberta introduced its own licensed online gambling framework in 2026. In the US, it gets even more convoluted. While some states allow online bingo or gambling, others impose stricter laws. The operators need to be aware of local laws instead of assuming that a license in one state will automatically give them the authority to run a gambling operation in any other state. Europe is just as varied. Countries such as Sweden, Spain and Germany have their own licensing systems and requirements. So a bingo site operating in several European markets may need to meet quite different standards. More Than Just Calling Numbers The social aspect of bingo contributes almost as much to its attractiveness as the game itself. Traditional bingo halls are meeting spots, places for conversation, camaraderie and socialisation and hence it is no wonder that the UK Government pr

item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
item.description: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. item.title: ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region. Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and flag-off of special intervention projects by the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) in Borno State. He recalled that Tinubu played a significant role in securing the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket for former President Muhammadu Buhari ahead of the 2015 general election. According to the vice president, Tinubu deliberately moved the party’s presidential primary to Lagos and mobilised support for Buhari in the South-West, contributing to his emergence as the party’s candidate. “Those of us that were active in the political scene can bear testimony to the fact that without the efforts of President Bola Tinubu, Muhammadu Buhari couldn’t have clinched the ticket of the APC in 2014 in Lagos. “He deliberately shifted the base of the primaries to Lagos, and he worked assiduously to deliver the South-West. And one good turn always deserves another,” Shettima said. ﻿ The vice president urged the people of the North to reciprocate Tinubu’s political support by backing his re-election, declaring that the region had an opportunity to return the favour. “And for us in the North, this is payback time. I urge you, I beseech all of us here, let us use our informed judgment and make decisions that are in the best interest of our nation,” he said. Making a case for the administration’s economic policies, Shettima urged Nigerians to consider the government’s economic performance when deciding who to support in the 2027 elections. He cited a decline in headline inflation and an increase in the country’s foreign reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 17 years. “The economy has turned the corner. Headline inflation has come down. Our foreign reserve is the highest in the past 17 years. It’s now hovering in the region of 55 billion dollars,” he said. Defending the removal of the petrol subsidy, the vice president maintained that the decision was not intended to worsen the economic hardship faced by Nigerians but to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing. “And the President has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy not to inflict pain on Nigerians, no. He removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. item.title: Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real
item.description: Porsche provided flights from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 718 EV prototype. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. It wasn't until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche's upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle. That's not particularly low for a sports car, but it's practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that's usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed. So, for the company's first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance. item.title: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in New York from 2027

My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said. In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. item.title: Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The company’s blog post cites 236 accounts. Because Coldcard is self-custodial, Coinkite can only count losses that customers report, and it says the true number is likely higher. The report cites Galaxy Research figures showing 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, worth about $107 million at today’s price. Galaxy pegged losses above $115 million in August, based on prices when the coins were taken, and white hats later moved some exposed coins into a recovery trust. Who found and exploited the flaw is still unknown, and law enforcement is investigating. The report calls AI

item.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
item.description: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government ( PDF ). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations." The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China's lunar ambitions are as expansive as NASA's, and there is a good chance the country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there. item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Stacks Opens Bond 4 With 1,050 BTC of Bitcoin Staking Capacity GRAND CAYMAN, Cayman Islands, Nov. 24, 2026. Stacks Labs today announced 1,050 BTC of capacity for Bond 4 of Bitcoin staking with Stacks, a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. The bond starts ~Dec. 5, and institutions can register at stacks.co/institutional-bitcoin-staking. Bond 4 carries a 3% target annual yield, paid in BTC weekly over a six-month term. Each BTC staked is paired with STX worth 5% of its value, so filling Bond 4’s 1,050 BTC of capacity requires a corresponding STX commitment. Rewards come from Stacks miners, who commit BTC through Proof of Transfer (PoX), the consensus mechanism Stacks has run since January 2021. Every bond since the Genesis Bond launched in September has filled. 21shares returned for Bond 3, and Bullish (NYSE: BLSH) joined as the first top-10 public Bitcoin treasury company to stake BTC. “Opening more than 1,000 BTC of new capacity for institutions shows how strong the demand for Bitcoin yield has become,” said Muneeb Ali, CEO, Stacks Labs, and founder of Stacks. Institutions can stake from qualified custody, including BitGo. During the bootstrap phase, self-custodial Bitcoin staking is whitelisted. Holders who are not on the whitelist can take part through pooled Bitcoin staking at stacks.co/bitcoin-staking . About Stacks Stacks is a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. With Bitcoin staking, holders stake BTC with STX, and their BTC stays on the Bitcoin L1 under their own custody. Stacks has distributed over 4,200 BTC in rewards to participants since 2021. Learn more at stacks.co . Media contact: Shannon Voight, PR & Events, Stacks Labs, press@stackslabs.com Institutional onboarding: https://www.stacks.co/institutional-bitcoin-staking Disclaimer : This is a sponsored press release. item.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
item.description: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo , took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans. A handful of teeth with a lot to say Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth. Read full article Comments

item.title: NDC Boycotts IGP’s Meeting Over Alleged Attacks On Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures. The party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks on its members allegedly carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The NDC announced its position in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday. It said it would not legitimise a security process that had failed to protect its members, adding that the alleged violence had become an intolerable pattern across the country. The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Calabar, Enugu and Delta states, including an alleged attempt by APC loyalists to prevent its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State. It accused the APC-led government of turning political campaigns into battlefields, where the safety of opposition members could no longer be guaranteed. The NDC also alleged that security personnel were complicit in the violence, particularly the alleged attack on the campaign team of its Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State. Omo-Agege is a chieftain of the NDC. Gunmen reportedly attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area. The former deputy senate president escaped unhurt, according to his media adviser, Sunny Areh. The attack initially left four campaign members dead, according to the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation. However, the Nigeria Police Force said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed, while several others sustained injuries. Police Speak The police, in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Force Public Relations Officer, said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and determine the verified casualty figure. Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. The police said the investigation would examine the sequence of events, identify those responsible and establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. It added that any officer found to have acted negligently or breached professional standards would face disciplinary action, while anyone found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted. The NDC, however, accused the police of displaying bias and failing to investigate previous attacks on its members or bring those responsible to justice. item.title: NASA’s Titan-Bound Dragonfly Rotorcraft Gets Its Eyes
item.description: Science instruments for NASA’s Dragonfly are starting to arrive at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, where the car-sized rotorcraft is coming together for its mission to explore Saturn’s largest moon, Titan. From left, technicians Chad Cook and Seth Harvey install the high-resolution microscopic imager – part of the seven-camera DragonCam science imaging suite – onto NASA’s Dragonfly rotorcraft at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, on Nov. 6, 2026. NASA/Johns Hopkins APL/Ed Whitman First to check in: DragonCam, which consists of seven cameras designed to characterize Titan ’s surface at multiple scales during flight and while on the ground. By mid-November, all seven cameras developed and built by Malin Space Science Systems had been installed in their insulated housings, tested, and integrated into the rotorcraft. Each camera will look out at Titan through a window in a foam enclosure that insulates the cameras and Dragonfly’s interior from Titan’s cryogenic environment, where ambient temperatures reach minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit. A configurable LED array, built at APL and spanning the light spectrum from the infrared to the ultraviolet, provides information about the color of surface materials at the sampling site and helps scientists make inferences about their composition. During Titan’s long night, which spans nearly eight Earth days, these observations also may allow DragonCam to identify organic molecules that fluoresce under ultraviolet light. The LED illumination also allows us to see Titan as human eyes would. “One of the most exciting things about Dragonfly is that we’ll be able to see Titan from perspectives we’ve never had before,” said Elizabeth Turtle, Dragonfly principal investigator at APL. “With the capability to take images when Dragonfly is on the surface as well as while flying, DragonCam will give us both detailed views and sweeping panoramas of Titan’s landscape, as well as insight into the processes that shaped this extraordinary world. Seeing these cameras become part of the Dragonfly lander is an exciting milestone that brings us another step closer to this unprecedented exploration.” Matthew Clark (left) and Michael Ravine of Malin Space Science Systems check DragonCam’s seven science cameras and digital video recorder before shipping them to Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) for integration and testing onto NASA’s Dragonfly rotorcraft. MSSS/Olawale Oluwo In addition to these science cameras, Dragonfly has two navigation cameras, also built by Malin Space Science Systems, that were installed this summer. “We are extremely pleased to have delivered the DragonCam cameras,” said Michael Ravine, DragonCam development manager and a Dragonfly co-investigator from Malin Space Science Systems. “Now to have them on the Dragonfly spacecraft, taking images, it’s so much easier to picture how they will work on Titan. item.title: YunLone Galaxy star projector review — a sub-$30 customizable night light
item.description: null The YunLone Galaxy Projector is an inexpensive but effective way to bring the marvel of space into your living room or bedroom. Costing around $28, this star projector can display beautiful dancing auroras across your walls and ceiling, and thanks to app support, a huge range of color options are available. In fact, the color combinations you can display here are almost infinite. Key specs Size: 3.54 x 3.15 x 4.72 inches (9 x 8 x 12 cm) Weight: 17.6 ounces (500 g) Bulb Type: LED Laser: Yes Operation: App and remote control Rotation: Yes Sleep timer: Yes Speaker: Yes With built-in sounds, a Bluetooth speaker and endless customization options, this really is an all-singing, all-dancing star projector. We're amazed at just how much is loaded into this package for such a low price. It's surprisingly good quality, too, with the unit itself being sturdy and made out of hard-wearing plastic. This isn't a scientific star projector, of course. For that, we'd recommend the Sega Toys Homestar Classic or the Hommkiety Galaxy Projector . But even though the YunLone Galaxy Projector won't give you an accurate view of the Northern Hemisphere's night sky or a close-up of the moon, it's still a projector we recommend. If you're looking to create a relaxing atmosphere, it's one of the best star projectors we've reviewed. YunLone Galaxy Projector: Design The Yunlone Galaxy Projector has a simple but effective design. Kim Snaith The Yunlone Galaxy Projector has a simple but effective design. Kim Snaith Solid build quality Functional rather than aesthetic design Limited buttons on the front of the unit The YunLone Galaxy Projector doesn't have the most attractive design: It's clearly built for functionality rather than aesthetics. You won't find nearly as many functions as the YunLone Galaxy Projector packs in, however. That isn't to say that the YunLone Galaxy Projector is ugly, though. The design is basic, with a circular shape that houses a clear globe in the middle that acts as the projector. It sits on rubberized feet, so it doesn't easily slip or move around, and it's naturally tilted, so it points slightly diagonally rather than straight up. Given the wide reach of the projector, it helps spread the aurora lights across your entire room. The projector has a solid build quality: It's plastic but feels sturdy and well-made. If you're buying for a child's bedroom, you don't need to worry about little hands being too rough when using it. item.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
item.description: null (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system. Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Why is it incredible? For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth. But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid , meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet. Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

item.title: UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65% UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country. The six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit said in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026. The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported . How the certificate works A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself. If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years. That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default. “With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit. “Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.” Built on notes sold in Germany and Austria Di Stasi said the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead. HypoVereinsbank, UniCredit’s German unit, sold a version to private clients in March with a 160% cap, or 60% upside. UniCredit Bank Austria launched its own six-year note in April with a 175% cap, or 75% upside. Italy’s 65% falls between the two. The bank has moved into bitcoin in steps. It first offered a capital-protected bitcoin product to professional clients only in 2025. In May, it placed a bitcoin and ether certificate for professional clients with a €100,000 minimum. item.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. The post Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20% South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups issue won stablecoins. The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users. Lee said the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted quickly. A 20% ownership cap for exchanges Under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market. Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. Existing exchanges would get three years after designation to comply, and small and midsize exchanges could get up to three more. The cap could reach some of Korea’s best-known exchanges. Mirae Asset Consulting owns 97.15% of Digital X, the exchange formerly known as Korbit, The Korea Herald reported . Naver Financial’s planned share-swap takeover of Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, would make the exchange a wholly owned subsidiary. The FSC declined to comment on specific companies, the paper said. “Ownership restrictions are necessary to strengthen exchanges’ public accountability and neutrality,” Yoo Young-jun, director general of the FSC’s Digital Financial Policy Bureau, said at a briefing, citing more than 10 million exchange accounts in Korea. The bill would also move trade execution, listing reviews and market surveillance from self-regulation to formal rules. Exchanges would need outside directors to make up a majority of their boards, plus audit committees and compliance officers. Coin offerings and won stablecoins Domestic initial coin offerings would be allowed as long as issuers file a white paper with the FSC before marketing tokens to the public. The release pointed to a platform company that sidestepped Korea’s ICO ban by setting up a foundation abroad, then sold its token through local exchanges. Exchanges would have to file and publish a report on each token they list. item.title: DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move. The complaint , filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft. On Nov. 12, the department said it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day. Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds. Circle will mint replacement tokens Circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control. Instead, Circle has agreed to issue new USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.” Several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint says. How the Binance hack worked The filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange said earlier this month. The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors said the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived. The first large transfer, about $780 million in USDC, left Binance on Ethereum at about 4:41 p.m. ET on Oct. 29, the complaint says. Another $43 million followed 18 minutes later. Investigators also traced AVAX that was split up, bridged and swapped until it became about $1.56 million in USDC. U.S. agencies attribute the theft to North Korean military hackers known as the Lazarus Group, or APT38. Investigators said some wallets that collected Binance funds also received money from the roughly $387 million Bitget hack in September, which the exchange’s CEO tied to North Korea. item.title: Inside the 2026 WISCAR Mentoring Walk
item.description: Mentors, mentees, professionals and members of the public gathered at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for the annual Women in Successful Careers (WISCAR) Mentoring Walk . Led by WISCAR Founder and Chairperson, Amina Oyagbola , the walk forms part of the lead-up to the organisation’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference. Participants were paired up for the walk along the Eko Atlantic, each with someone they had not met before. At the end of the route, they switched to new mentor-mentee partners for a short mentoring session, which gave everyone two fresh conversations in one morning. Back at the meeting point, participants shared what they had learnt from their partners, from career advice to personal lessons. Nutritionist Sherese Ijewere then led a session on healthy eating and answered questions on everyday food choices. Coach Bobbie Tee of Happy Heart Fitness, closed the morning with a Zumba session. Next stop: the conference The walk sets the stage for WISCAR’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference , themed “ Courage in Action: Shaping Policies and Structures for Inclusive Progress. ” The conference takes place on Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Lagos. Highlights include: A keynote from Dr Ndidi Nwuneli , former President and CEO of the ONE Campaign and Founder of LEAP Africa, who will also receive this year’s Distinguished WISCAR Award. Speakers including Badejo-Okusanya , SAN, President of the Nigerian Bar Association, and Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, President of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management (CIPM) The launch of WISCAR’s CIPM-endorsed Corporate Mentoring Playbook The graduation of Cohort 2 of the Women in Law Mentoring Programme Register now at https://wiscar.ng/almc . item.title: China launching 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station today: Watch it live
item.description: null China will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live. A Long March 2F rocket is scheduled to launch the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25). You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong , a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022. Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight will make history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who will be the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023 .) China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025 , with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training. We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch. This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest. Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu. Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24 . According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.
